fields.summary: A user can edit the commit message when merging a pull request
fields.description: When merging a pull request, it would be useful to be able to edit the commit message for the pull request merge.

comments.body:
We should have:

* textfield for the subject line (summary or subject)
* textarea for the extended commit message

The subject line should be limited to ~120 characters (maxlength) but we should encourage shorter subjects (e.g. have a counter that changes colours if the subject exceeds 60 characters (?))
It should be possible to properly wrap the extended commit message (see Linus' epic rant on GH: https://github.com/torvalds/linux/pull/17#issuecomment-5659933)

Good commit messages should be a) possible and b) encouraged

Resources:
* http://www.kernel.org/pub/software/scm/git/docs/git-commit.html ("Though not required, it’s a good idea to begin the commit message with a single short (less than 50 character) line summarizing the change, followed by a blank line and then a more thorough description. Tools that turn commits into email, for example, use the first line on the Subject: line and the rest of the commit in the body.")
* http://tbaggery.com/2008/04/19/a-note-about-git-commit-messages.html

Makes it play nicely with for example

* git shortlog
* git show
* git format-patch
* git log --format=(oneline|email)
* any other command that supports {{--format}} or {{--pretty}}

This is extremely important for us. As JIRA will not pick up merge commits unless you put the special tags in the commit message. This is important for us to ensure that a ticket has been properly merged into all of the baselines. It would be nice if Stash could automatically add the ticket IDs to the merge commit message based on the existing commit messages.

[~afinnell] what if JIRA would show pull requests and their merge commits without needing to specify the issue key in the commit message. Presumably this would solve your problem _and_ remove a manual step during development of a feature.
That would solve the issue. It would need to handle multiple issue keys in one pull request though. We sometimes fix multiple tickets in a single branch.

Our company use SVN as a head SCM system, and unfortunately it won't be changed.
My team is using Git locally, and syncing changes from Git to SVN. It works great, but i can't automate this process since a nasty SVN policy - a commit message should have Jira-Id strictly at the beginning, otherwise the server won't accept a commit (for example "STASH-1234 a bugfix").
When we do merging in git (via Stash pull request), we get such merge message "Merge pull request #44 from ... to ...", and, obviously during a sync to SVN those merges get rejected.
So getting back to point - i really need this feature - to be able to edit commit message for a pull request either via web interface or a hook, to comply with our Svn rules.
I agree, we integrate our time tracking with Redmine and without the ability to modify the commit messages for pull requests our spent times are counted double.
Any update on this?
Sorry Alan, no update on this yet.

This would be a really useful feature.

It would allow me to:
1) Hide separate commits for a feature from our customers that have access to the source (I really don't want them to see all the corrections that were made after reviews/testing)
2) When annotating files, easily see the feature the change belonged to (instead of 'Merge PR from xxx')

It would even be good if there was just an option to use the first commit message in the feature branch for the pull request merge.

This would be great for us as we want to use meaningful commit message on merge to autogenerate release notes - i.e. we get one commit message on master per feature, and it discusses what we did in business terms

We use FishEye smart commits extensively for time tracking, so this is really a blocker for us adopting Stash for pull request-based workflow. All of our developers' time gets "double-booked" on the merge commit. We can't use pull requests + merge, and thus are under-utilizing Stash, until this is resolved.


Is there any work-around for this in the meantime, i.e. can we set the equivalent of {{git config --global merge.log=false}}?

Hi Noah,

Unfortunately setting the config option globally won't work as we explicitly set the log option on {{git merge}}.
So unfortunately there currently is no workaround. I think STASH-3529 is describing your problem. As Jens pointed out on that issue it would most likely be a trade-off between not interfering with smart commits and linking the merge commit correctly against JIRA issues so editing the commit message before merging may be the best middle ground here.

So unfortunately I don't have a solution for you right now but we'll look into this or STASH-3529 to figure out how we can address this.

Cheers,
Stefan

Another option (which I'm seriously considering, if Atlassian cannot prioritize this issue), is to write a post-receive git hook that logs work via the JIRA rest API.  I posted a question for this idea on Atlassian Answers: https://answers.atlassian.com/questions/291403/poor-man-s-smart-commits-in-stash-using-post-receive-git-hook
This should be pretty useful when using the option to «squash» a pull request.

Changing a merge commit message seems to be a very simple feature, even Gitlab has it.
Having specific information in merge commit messages might be required for traceability, so you can understand when specific task was fixed by using only a git log.
I would also love to see this feature!
+1  - we have a format for doing merge commits, and automation that keys off that like I imagine a lot of people.
This is absolutely crucial to anyone using squash merge strategy. Is this any where close to being implemented?

We also need this since we have a validation formatting the merge commit. Our plugin isn't doing anything now because we can't modify the merge message. Also, the pull request description is editable, in order for the users to add useful information, but that is lost once is it merged since it is not kept in the merge commit message.

We also have teams that want to use squash strategy which is not feasible without this. But also for those who keep the feature branches this would be interesting. 

Please implement this!

We also have teams that want to use squash strategy which is not feasible without this. But also for those who keep the feature branches this would be interesting.
Please implement this!

Title and description have to be entered already when creating a pull request, but they do not end up in final merge commit message. This does not make much sense to me. The generated text of the merge commit is useless, use title and description of the pull request instead. Please solve this issue.
We also have users who report to me that at Bitbucket the title of the pull requests is written in the commit message and in stash not... So, i vote also for the comment from @Jens Weiske. Thanks

In Stash 3.7 (not yet released as at 2015-02-19) we've introduced the ability to _add_ text to the pull request merge commit message. This text will appear between the subject line and the log lines that Stash/git generates. We have a separate feature request that we are still considering for including the pull request title/description (STASH-2894).

Once this feature is available and people are familiar with using it we'd love to hear feedback on how it's working for you.

I hate to be the first one to complain but why only go half way? One of the most important pieces to edit is the subject line of the commit, as that is the first thing you usually see in most tooling. The detail / body section is hidden away.

Thanks for the early feedback! From the input we had at the time I didn't believe leaving the subject line intact would be contentious. The reason for doing it this way is that the subject line provides the only link back to the pull request that created it, and we didn't want to mess up processes that depend on that.

We'll continue to gather feedback and as always are open to making adjustments in a future release, so please keep it coming.

@Roger That's more or less metadata only relevant to Stash as far as I'm concerned and doesn't belong in the subject line. An ideal scenario would be for us to have control over the subject line *and* the body. All stash would do is place a single line of metadata as the last line of the body. In this line of text you can put whatever you want: pull request number, branch name, etc.

Fully agree with previous posters. Because of complying with IEEE standards we need full control over the subject line for traceability. Without full control this feature does not have value to us and we cannot move to Stash.
Strong agreement with Alexander Rupsch summary

Agree with previous posters. The subject line it the most important one and without control over it this feature does not make any sense.

@Roger: People who rely on subject line containing can always just keep default message, without editing it. Then all their current processes will continue to work, while you still give enough flexibility for people needing it. ~and you always can add configuration to disable manual editing of such messages~

When you say "This text will appear between the subject line and the log lines that Stash/git generates.", what do you mean exactly? From what I understand, the "subject line" is the "message" field when consulting the commits list, and is at the top under the author when consulting the commit's details page. The "log lines" are only in the commit's details page, composed of the commit id used for the merge and a list of descriptions from the commits contained in the pull request. You added the possibility to add text only in the commit's details page between those two? Did I understand correctly? I would have preferred being able to change the subject line so the message appears in the commits list page.

If that's the case, when can that text be added? At any moment? Can we make it so that the pull request description is added there automatically when merging? If I write a Jira Ticket in that field, will it appear in the "Issues" column of the commits list page? Will that field be made available in the Changeset java object in the API so we can read/write the contents? Can we have a release candidate to try the function out? 

Sorry for asking a lot of questions.

In my opinion the whole commit message should be configurable, or at the very least the subject line (what follows is less important). I think people have different needs for the subject line. 

Ours is that we would like it to contain the JIRA issue key and the pull request title (not the JIRA issue title as it can be in a different language) in some predefined format, for example "JIRA-123: Added some new cool feature". I do not like the fact that every user performing the merge could affect the format of the subject line. It will result in multiple formatting being used because people cannot remember the convention. 

For some, editing may be useful. Therefore there should be a toggle where you can either enable edit just before merge or disallow it altogether. In addition there should be a template for defining the default value (which would be automatically used if editing is disabled).

At the moment when we squash all commits in the merge, the commit message only gives us the JIRA issue key from the branch name. It's not really useful as you always need to go to JIRA to decode that issue key.

As a workaround for people who need absolute control over the merge log messages, users with push access to the target branch can merge the PR source branch at the command line, push and stash will close the pull request as an "external merge".

It's a bit of a hack, but I use it occasionally to bypass restrictions on pull requests when meeting them is... inconvenient :)
[~jpoh],[~nhansberry],[~mmcglynn],[~bplump] is it possible to update user message in GitPullRequestMergeRequestedEvent or somewhere else through stash API?

Any update on this?  Currently Pull Request adds the latest commit message from FromRef as default title which gets added to pull request commit message, nothing changes even if the pull request title is edited before merge.   

Is there a way we can edit pull request commit message?
[~kalpanasanthi.raju11440659204], you can edit the commit message at merge time in Stash 3.7+ and Bitbucket Server 4.x+

@Roger_Barnes, we are using Bitbucket Server 4.6+ and are only able to add to the commit message, but not edit the pre-defined commit message which seems to be the spirit of this request. Is there a way to edit the entire message, including the Bitbucket generated summary line?

I was wondering that too (edit the actual commit message).

Also, I was wondering if there was a way to access that new feature through the Atlassian SDK. By that, I mean do a kind of "merge check" when the merge window is open and the user can edit that commit message, like described in my question [here|https://answers.atlassian.com/questions/39786112/merge-pull-request-window-check-and-veto]
[~dustyn1997383316], [~a_silversword], BSERV-8384 tracks the suggested improvement to allow editing of the entire message.

"A user can edit the commit message when merging a pull request"
 "Fixed": user can't edit the message at all, just append to it...

Would make more sense if instead of appending to the message you could prepend to it, or have a setting for append/prepend.
 I hope BSERV-2894 and/or BSERV-8384 could be implemented some day.

On Bitbucket server 4.11, this issue is still active (why is it closed here ???) ! Nothing has been fixed, and editing just partially the commit message is really not enough. Configure append/prepend message, or at least the whole message should really be done
[~nicholas.jallan314509068], BSERV-8384 tracks the suggested improvement to allow editing of the entire message.

fields.summary: Be able to query Epic assignment history of all issues ever assigned with an Epic
fields.description:
COS: 
- For a given epic return the history of all issues added and removed (with time) from the Epic
- Will need to inform admins that they need to re-index
- This does not involve the addition of JQL to assist in this querying

(!) Development Notes (!)

Q: I'm assuming this will only be seen on the view issue page?
A: It won't be seen in the UI anywhere. It will only be seen by accessing the URL directly. 

Q: What if the epic has been deleted?
A: You get an error message: issue does not exist. 

Q: What if the epic was converted to an issue/subtask?
A: It doesn't check. If you changed it in JIRA and there are still epic child links, you'll still see the data.

Q: What if the linked issue was moved/converted/deleted?
A: It should still show up in the appropriate group (incomplete, complete, punted)

Q: From what version forward will we be tracking this history? aka if an epic link already existed before we introduce this change?
A: previous epic links should be tracked

Q: Do any of these questions surprise you? If so, what hadn't you previously considered?
A: the first one, because it's not a UI story

Q: What else can you think of?
A: (x) Not Answered

The output of this story is a REST service accessed by the URL: 
http://(JIRA-URL)/rest/greenhopper/1.0/rapid/charts/epicreport/(rapid view ID)/(epic key)

e.g. http://localhost:2990/jira/rest/greenhopper/1.0/rapid/charts/epicreport/5/FULL-5

Tools to easily view the json
============================= 
JSON View for Chome: 
https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/jsonview/chklaanhfefbnpoihckbnefhakgolnmc?hl=en

PrettyJson for Sublime 
======================
https://github.com/dzhibas/SublimePrettyJson
(v easy install)

Created a new rest URL for this report (see last comment)

Please test by adding / removing stories from epics, change story status, different status mappings, different fields for estimation, etc. 

Does not account for changes in estimates.
